A_target.statement:
The number of [[Definition:Labeled Tree|labeled trees]] on $n$ [[Definition:Vertex of Graph|vertices]] is:
:$n^{n - 2}$

B_source.statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be [[Definition:Finite Set|finite sets]].
If there exists a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] $\phi: S \to T$, then:
:$\card S = \card T$

substitutions.the set of known size: sequences of length n minus two over an alphabet of n symbols
substitutions.the encoding map: repeatedly remove the smallest leaf and record its neighbour
substitutions.the decoding map: reconstruct the tree from the sequence by reversing the removals

derived.the bijection between the two sets: labelled trees correspond to Prufer sequences
derived.the cardinality transferred: n to the power n minus two

validity_conditions: The encoding is well defined because every tree with at least two vertices has a leaf, so the removal process runs to completion.
The decoding is well defined because at each stage the next leaf to be removed is determined by the remaining sequence, which makes the two maps mutually inverse.
Both directions must be checked; exhibiting only an injection would give an inequality rather than the exact count.
proof_plan:
Given a labeled tree $T$ on $\set {1, \ldots, n}$, repeatedly delete the [[Definition:Leaf of Tree|leaf]] with the smallest label and record its unique neighbour, until two vertices remain.
This gives the [[Definition:Prüfer Sequence|Prüfer sequence]] of $T$.
The sequence has length $n - 2$, with entries in $\set {1, \ldots, n}$.

Conversely, from a sequence $\tuple {a_1, \ldots, a_{n - 2} }$, reconstruct $T$ by joining at each step the smallest label not yet used and not appearing in the remaining sequence to $a_i$.
The encoding and decoding maps are [[Definition:Inverse Mapping|mutually inverse]].

Hence the Prüfer encoding is a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] onto $\set {1, \ldots, n}^{n - 2}$, and the number of labeled trees is $n^{n - 2}$.
{{qed}}
